To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) The cross sections of reactions with heavy projectiles can be predicted with an accuracy of a few orders of magnitude, provided that the experimental data are sufficiently abundant.
the cross sections of the reactions leading to superheavy elements are very large, and the formation of superheavy nuclei is possible at the present day accelerators.

the theoretical predictions of cross sections of superheavy elements can be made with a precision of a factor of 10, provided that the experimental data are also precise enough, and that the theoretical calculations of cross sections of the reactions of interest should be performed with the most recent codes, which are able to account for the effects of nuclear deformation, and which are based on the most recent nuclear potentials and nuclear structure models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of new elements in the region of the superheavy nuclei and the study of their properties.
the synthesis of the superheavy nuclei in the region of Z=114 and A=294, which is a region where the nuclear shell effects are expected to be most pronounced.
theoretical problems in synthesis of superheavy elements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the theoretical description of the reaction mechanism of heavy-ion induced fusion reactions is in a state where predictions of the absolute cross sections are not possible with sufficient accuracy.
the present state of theoretical understanding of the synthesis of superheavy elements does not permit a reliable prediction of cross sections for any particular reaction.

, in spite of the progress in theoretical description of heavy ion reactions, a reliable prediction of absolute values of cross-sections for the production of superheavy nuclei is still not possible. A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the theoretical prediction of cross section for superheavy elements is still in a developing stage.
we have been able to predict the cross sections for the production of the superheavy nuclei up to Z=117 with reasonable accuracy.

the cross sections of fusion-evaporation reactions are predicted with an accuracy of about a factor of two, while the cross sections of deep inelastic collisions are predicted with an uncertainty of about an order of magnitude, and the cross sections of quasifission reactions are predicted with a factor of about 100.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reaction mechanism is still not fully understood, especially in the case of the fusion reaction.
the cross section for the synthesis of a given superheavy element depends strongly on the choice of nuclear model used in the calculations.
the reaction mechanisms are not fully understood and that the cross section calculations are still very much model dependent.
